notes: Program availability can change, and calling does not guarantee immediate housing or an opening.
description: Clackamas County's central access point for people experiencing a housing crisis. Staff screen the situation, connect callers with housing or homelessness services, and explain possible next steps.
eligibility_summary: People in Clackamas County who are homeless or facing a housing crisis. Program availability and individual eligibility vary.

program_name: Clackamas County Housing Rights and Resources Program
notes: This program provides information and referrals. Contact the program to confirm what assistance is appropriate for your situation.
description: Provides general housing information and referrals about landlord-tenant issues, fair housing, housing rights, and lower-cost housing options in Clackamas County.
eligibility_summary: Community members in Clackamas County who need housing-rights information, fair-housing guidance, landlord-tenant referrals, or help locating lower-cost housing. The county does not state an income requirement on the program page.

program_name: Area Agency on Aging and Disabilities of SW WA - Housing Info
notes: Serves Clark, Klickitat, Skamania, Cowlitz, and Wahkiakum counties.
description: Information and assistance for seniors and people with disabilities.
eligibility_summary: Seniors or adults with disabilities.

notes: Open Monday–Friday, 9 AM–4 PM. Call or visit the center to ask which benefits, supplies, or financial programs fit your situation.
description: A resource center that helps Clark County veterans and their families connect with benefits, financial aid, food, clothing, hygiene supplies, and gear for veterans living outside.
eligibility_summary: Veterans and their families in Clark County. Eligibility varies by service; contact the center for current requirements.

notes: No appointment is required; walk-ins are first come, first served. Fund hours are Monday–Friday, 9 AM–3 PM, and late arrivals may not be accommodated. Assistance is limited and conditions can change.
description: Limited financial help for qualified low-income veterans, including eviction prevention, rent or a security deposit with a housing voucher, utilities, transportation, prescriptions, and other approved needs.
eligibility_summary: Qualified low-income veterans who currently live in Clark County and can document one continuous year of Washington residency. Bring a DD-214 and the last 30 days of household-income verification; additional documents are required for spouses and dependents.

cost_details: Financial assistance depends on eligibility and available funds. Contact the utility for the amount and conditions; no benefit is guaranteed.
program_name: Clark Public Utilities - Operation Warm Heart
notes: Call 360-992-3000 to request help. This program addresses electric heating bills; the source does not establish a general utility setup or deposit benefit.
description: Electric heating bill assistance for qualifying Clark Public Utilities customers facing financial hardship. Contact the utility to ask about eligibility and available help.
eligibility_summary: Clark Public Utilities customers struggling to pay electric heating bills, particularly households that do not qualify for other energy assistance. Eligibility is income-based; call the utility for screening.

program_name: Council for the Homeless - Housing Hotline
notes: Primary entry point for all Clark County shelter and housing programs. · How to apply: Call 360-695-9677 (M-F 9am-8pm, Weekends 11am-5pm).
description: Centralized intake for emergency shelter and housing assistance in Clark County.
eligibility_summary: Clark County residents experiencing or at risk of homelessness.

program_name: Inter-Faith Treasure House – Rent and Utility Assistance
notes: Funding and geographic eligibility can change; call before visiting or submitting documents. · How to apply: Call the Interfaith Treasure House office at 360-834-4181 to ask whether assistance is currently available.
description: Provides limited emergency assistance with rent and utility payments when funding is available. Inter-Faith Treasure House also operates a food bank and offers household goods and other basic-needs support for residents of the Camas and Washougal area. Call to confirm available assistance and current hours.
eligibility_summary: Residents of Camas, Washougal, and eastern Clark County, generally including ZIP codes 98607, 98671, and the eastern portion of 98683. Assistance depends on the household’s need and available funding.

notes: Call the Housing Solutions Center for referral details and current availability. The Nest is a housing-support program, not a walk-in emergency shelter.
description: A six-month program that provides move-in financial assistance and case management to young adults preparing to live independently.
eligibility_summary: Young adults ages 18–24 who are ready to live independently but cannot afford the initial move-in costs of an apartment. The Housing Solutions Center determines referral eligibility.

cost_details: $100 nonrefundable processing fee. Delivery costs an additional $150; beds, mattresses and box springs have separate charges.
notes: The bank does not provide help paying its fees. Delivery is generally limited to about 20 miles from its locations and cannot cross into Oregon. Tacoma: 253-302-3868. If collecting furniture, arrange a suitable vehicle and confirm pickup requirements.
description: Furniture for people who have stable housing but lack essential furnishings. An approved community partner must refer you to the Tacoma or Vancouver furniture bank.
eligibility_summary: People in stable housing who need basic furniture and have an approved agency referral. Serves Pierce, South King, Clark and Cowlitz counties; not all of King County. Delivery eligibility depends on the address.

notes: Families are referred by local agencies, community partners, and churches. Call 360-737-0300 for current availability and next steps; space is limited.
description: A Christian residential shelter for families with children that provides housing, food, basic necessities, case management, life-skills support, and help moving toward independence.
eligibility_summary: Families with children experiencing homelessness who are willing to participate in the program. Acceptance depends on available space and an intake with the case-management team.

program_name: Salvation Army Washougal Rent and Utility Assistance
notes: Assistance is limited and availability can change; contact the local corps before traveling. · How to apply: Call 360-835-3171 to confirm current funding, service-area eligibility, and application steps.
description: Emergency rent and utility assistance for residents of Camas and Washougal when funding is available.
eligibility_summary: Residents of the Camas and Washougal service area; the provider confirms current requirements.
source_type: Official provider and city resource guide

notes: Call the Housing Solutions Center at 360-695-9677 for assessment and referral. SHARE does not accept direct applications for this program.
description: Provides housing assistance, case management, and connections to supportive services for individuals and families experiencing homelessness or at risk of losing their housing. Support may include housing planning, employment resources, budgeting, mental health services, domestic violence resources, childcare, and transportation. Applications must go through the Housing Solutions Center.
eligibility_summary: Individuals and families who are homeless or at risk of homelessness and have significant barriers to obtaining housing, such as illness, disability, or insufficient financial resources. Participants must be referred through the Housing Solutions Center.

program_name: SHARE House – Shelter for Single Men
notes: Call the Council for the Homeless Housing Solutions Center at 360-695-9677 for eligibility screening and shelter placement. Do not go directly to the shelter expecting a bed.
description: Emergency shelter in Vancouver for single men experiencing homelessness. SHARE House provides shelter with no stated limit on length of stay. Staff and housing navigators help residents address housing barriers, find permanent housing, and connect with employment, healthcare, education, and other community resources. Call the Housing Solutions Center for shelter access.
eligibility_summary: Single men experiencing homelessness. Eligibility and shelter placement are determined by the Council for the Homeless Housing Solutions Center.

notes: First apply for HEN through DSHS. After receiving a HEN referral, contact the Housing Solutions Center at 360-695-9677 for coordinated entry and assessment. A referral does not guarantee assistance because services depend on available funding.
description: Rapid-rehousing assistance for Clark County households experiencing homelessness who have been approved for Washington’s Housing and Essential Needs program. SHARE may provide emergency rental assistance, crisis management, hygiene and cleaning supplies, and transportation passes while the participant remains eligible and funding is available.
eligibility_summary: Washington residents experiencing homelessness who have a HEN referral from DSHS. DSHS generally requires applicants to be unable to work for at least 90 days because of a physical or mental condition, meet income and resource limits, and be at least 18, legally emancipated, or married. Final eligibility and referral are determined by DSHS.

program_name: St. Vincent de Paul at St. John – Rent and Utility Assistance
notes: Call Monday, Wednesday, or Friday from 9:30 AM–12:30 PM. Funding may not always be available.
description: Provides limited help with rent or utility payments when funding is available. Assistance is intended for residents of the St. John service area in central and northern Clark County. Call during assistance hours to ask about current funding and apply.
eligibility_summary: People living in Brush Prairie, north Orchards, north Hazel Dell, Salmon Creek, Hockinson, and other parts of central Clark County who need help paying rent or utilities. Assistance depends on available funding.

program_name: YWCA Clark County - SafeChoice Domestic Violence Program
notes: Call the local 24-hour hotline at 360-695-0501 or toll-free at 800-695-0167. The Main Street address is the community office; the emergency-shelter location is confidential.
description: Free, confidential domestic-violence support that includes a 24-hour crisis line, emergency shelter, safety planning, advocacy, supportive housing, and referrals.
eligibility_summary: People experiencing domestic violence. Services are available regardless of race, gender, religion, age, income, or sexuality.

notes: Contact a Regional Access Point listed on the official page. Walk-in capacity is limited, and Coordinated Entry does not guarantee a housing referral or placement.
description: Connects people experiencing homelessness in King County with assessment and possible referrals to rapid rehousing, transitional housing, permanent housing, and permanent supportive housing through Regional Access Points.
eligibility_summary: People experiencing homelessness in King County, including single adults, couples, families, veterans, people staying outside or in shelter, people fleeing violence, and some people leaving institutions. Young adults at risk of homelessness within 14 days may also qualify.

notes: Call 211, enter your ZIP code, and choose housing, shelter, or rent assistance. Housing is not immediately available, and each participating program has its own requirements.
description: Lane County's coordinated pathway to shelter, homelessness prevention, rent-assistance information, housing assessment, outreach, and referrals to participating housing programs.
eligibility_summary: People in Lane County who are experiencing homelessness, seeking shelter or housing, or at risk of losing their housing. Individual providers and programs determine final eligibility.

notes: Call the Shelter Access Line at 503-281-2442, extension 2, to ask about availability. Shelter locations are confidential.
description: Two confidential, gender-inclusive emergency shelters in Multnomah County for adults and children affected by domestic violence, with advocacy and basic-needs support for stays of up to 12 weeks.
eligibility_summary: Adults and children affected by domestic violence. A Safety Stabilization Assessment is required before shelter consideration, and placement depends on availability.

notes: Focuses on permanent supportive housing and wraparound services. · How to apply: Call 503-238-0705 or visit a Cascadia health center.
description: Provides home and community-based services, housing search, and placement.
eligibility_summary: Individuals with mental health challenges experiencing homelessness.

notes: Drop-in hours are Monday–Friday, 10 AM–1 PM, and no intake is needed for drop-in services. Call the program about housing support and current capacity.
description: Drop-in services, case management, and housing support for self-identified women experiencing homelessness, including showers, laundry, phone and computer access, information, and referrals.
eligibility_summary: Self-identified women age 25 or older who are experiencing homelessness and do not have children in their care. Contact the program to confirm eligibility for housing assistance.
address: 2740 SE Powell Boulevard, Suite 6, Portland, OR 97202

notes: Offers low-barrier, recovery, and supportive housing. · How to apply: Call (503) 525-8483 for assistance and current openings.
description: Centralized housing office for CCC's portfolio of over 2,300 units.
eligibility_summary: Very low-income individuals and families, often with barriers to housing.

program_name: Community for Positive Aging – Information and Assistance
notes: Call 503-288-8303 for help by phone or to make an appointment. This listing is for navigation and information, not a guaranteed housing placement or direct rent fund.
description: An Information and Assistance specialist helps older adults evaluate options and find resources for housing, caregiver needs, transportation, and other concerns.
eligibility_summary: Older adults and people seeking aging-related information or assistance. Contact staff to confirm eligibility for specific programs.

cost_details: Self-referral: $150 for furniture, plus $250 if delivery is needed. Agency support may cover fees; do not assume the service is free.
program_name: Community Warehouse - Furniture and Household Goods
notes: Furniture depends on donated inventory. Delivery of furniture is not a service for moving your existing household. Call or use the provider's contact page to arrange an appointment. Confirm service and delivery boundaries directly.
description: Furniture and household essentials for people setting up a home. Request an appointment yourself or through a partner agency at the Portland, Tigard or Gresham furniture bank.
eligibility_summary: People who lack essential furniture. A partner agency may help arrange access and cover fees. Self-referrals are also accepted; contact Community Warehouse to confirm your address and delivery options.

program_name: El Programa Hispano Católico - Housing Services
notes: For urgent rent, energy, or other immediate help, call 503-669-8350. The organization says it cannot respond to urgent-assistance requests by email. Funding and program openings can change.
description: Culturally specific housing-prevention and supportive services, including family stability, eviction support, emergency rental assistance, needs assessment, rapid rehousing, and housing placement and retention.
eligibility_summary: People with limited or no income who need housing help, are experiencing homelessness, or are at risk of homelessness. Requirements vary by program; the Family Stability program serves families with children under 18.

notes: Impact NW does not take direct applications for its housing programs. Use the official page to contact your county’s coordinated-access entry point. The Portland Worker of the Day program offers walk-up information and referrals, but it is not direct housing-program enrollment.
description: Prevention, rapid-rehousing, and permanent-supportive-housing programs for people experiencing homelessness or poverty. Program enrollment comes through county coordinated-access systems.
eligibility_summary: Individuals and families assessed and referred by coordinated access in Multnomah, Clackamas, Washington, or Clark County. Final eligibility depends on the specific program and available opening.

program_name: Independent Living Resources – Information and Referral
notes: Call 503-232-7411 to speak with an Information and Referral specialist. This service helps people navigate options; it is not a direct housing or rent fund.
description: Information and referral for people with disabilities who need help locating community resources, including housing, employment, financial assistance, and health care.
eligibility_summary: People with disabilities seeking information, referrals, advocacy, peer support, or independent-living services.

notes: Call first for screening. Screenings are available 365 days a year from 9 AM–5 PM. After 5 PM, the official page directs young adults needing a safe place to Porch Light at 1635 SW Alder Street at 8:45 PM.
description: The entry point for Portland’s Homeless Youth Continuum, providing screening and connections to shelter, housing, and other services for young adults experiencing homelessness.
eligibility_summary: Young adults ages 18–24 who are currently experiencing homelessness.

program_name: JOIN – Leasing and Housing Placement Support
notes: Participants are identified and referred through JOIN’s Placement and Retention teams. This is not a general online application program; contact JOIN for information about its current pathways.
description: Helps individuals and families overcome barriers to renting permanent housing. The program offers housing placement assistance, financial support, landlord coordination, and continued help securing and maintaining stable housing.
eligibility_summary: Individuals and families facing barriers to the traditional rental market, including low income, limited rental history, unstable employment, disability, immigration status, previous evictions, or justice-system involvement. Participants must be referred through JOIN’s Placement or Retention teams.

notes: Contact JOIN for current outreach availability. Outreach staff engage people on streets, in encampments, and in vehicles; this is not an emergency shelter or a guaranteed immediate placement.
description: Mobile outreach for people experiencing homelessness in Portland. JOIN staff meet people where they are—including on the streets, in encampments, and in vehicles—to build relationships, address barriers, connect them with resources, and support their transition into permanent housing.
eligibility_summary: Individuals and families experiencing homelessness in Portland, particularly people sleeping outside, in vehicles, or in encampments.

notes: NAYA’s Multnomah County emergency-rent-assistance referrals are currently closed; call 211 for that service. Families seeking Auntie’s Place shelter must be referred through Clackamas County Coordinated Housing Access. Call NAYA’s Housing Intake Coordinator to ask about other openings.
description: Culturally specific advocacy, longer-term housing stability assistance, shelter, and rapid rehousing for unhoused families.
eligibility_summary: Families of at least two people who are actively seeking permanent housing in the Portland area and have at least one household member who identifies as Native American or Alaska Native. Families with youth under 25 are prioritized.

program_name: New Avenues for Youth – Drop-In Day Services
notes: Call the Access Center at 503-432-3986 to complete screening. Check the official page for current Downtown and East Multnomah County locations and schedules. This is a day-service program, not an overnight shelter.
description: Day services for young people that include meals, showers, laundry, clothing, computers, internet, supportive advocates, activities, and connections to housing, education, employment, and other programs.
eligibility_summary: Young people ages 16–24 who complete screening through the Homeless Youth Continuum.

program_name: Our Just Future – Lilac Meadows Family Shelter
notes: There is no walk-in access. Call 211 for eligibility screening and coordinated intake into Multnomah County’s family shelter system.
description: Year-round emergency shelter in Southeast Portland for families experiencing homelessness. Lilac Meadows provides private rooms, meals, help accessing community services, and support finding permanent housing. There is no walk-in access; call 211 for screening and coordinated intake.
eligibility_summary: Families with one or more adults and at least one minor child, or individuals in their third trimester of pregnancy, who are experiencing homelessness. Eligibility and placement are determined through 211.

program_name: Outside In – Young Adult Day Program
notes: Call 503-432-3986 for Homeless Youth Continuum screening or visit the program to begin screening. Check the official page for current hours. This is a day program, not an overnight shelter.
description: A free day program with meals, showers, laundry, mail and internet access, case management, and help exploring transitional and community housing options.
eligibility_summary: Young adults ages 16–24 who have been screened into the Homeless Youth Continuum. Young adults may also visit to begin the screening process.
address: 1132 SW 13th Avenue, Second Floor, Portland, OR 97205

notes: Call 211 or text your ZIP code to 898211 and ask about family shelter. Path Home does not manage direct intake applications for Family Village.
description: A year-round, trauma-informed family shelter with private bedrooms, meals, basic-needs resources, case management, and help finding and retaining permanent housing.
eligibility_summary: Families who are currently experiencing homelessness and have children under age 18 in their care. Access is managed through 211.

notes: Email leasing@pcrihome.org, call 971-420-2213, or submit a paper application at PCRI’s office. This is for income-restricted affordable housing, not PCRI’s subsidized Section 8 list, which is closed.
description: Income-restricted affordable rental homes, primarily in North and Northeast Portland, with unit-specific limits at 30%, 50%, or 60% of area median income.
eligibility_summary: Households whose gross annual income is at or below the limit for the selected home. Income generally must equal at least 1.5 times the rent unless the household has a qualifying tenant-based voucher. Occupancy and screening rules also apply.
address: 6329 NE Martin Luther King Jr. Blvd, Portland, OR 97211

cost_details: Discount of 15% to 80% on eligible energy charges. This is not cash assistance, payment of earlier charges or a utility-deposit grant.
notes: Apply online or call PGE for help. PGE serves parts of seven Oregon counties, not every address in those counties. Other energy assistance may also be available; confirm options with the utility.
description: A discount on eligible electricity charges for qualifying Portland General Electric residential customers. Apply directly through PGE to reduce future energy charges.
eligibility_summary: Residential PGE customers who meet household income requirements. Your address must be served by PGE; living in a listed county alone does not qualify you.

program_name: Raphael House of Portland - Emergency Shelter
notes: Call the confidential 24-hour hotline at 503-222-6222 for safety planning, shelter information, and current screening availability. The shelter location is confidential.
description: An 11-room, confidential, gender-inclusive emergency shelter for adults, children, and pets fleeing intimate-partner violence, with round-the-clock advocacy and help moving toward stable housing.
eligibility_summary: Anyone impacted by domestic violence, regardless of gender identity, ethnicity, disability, immigration status, primary language, or sexuality. Shelter screening and space availability determine placement.

notes: Use the official property filters to view current vacancies and apply. Each property has separate eligibility requirements and availability.
description: A nonprofit affordable-housing provider with income-restricted apartments for individuals, families, seniors, veterans, and people with disabilities in Oregon and Southwest Washington.
eligibility_summary: Eligibility, income limits, age or program restrictions, and vacancy status vary by property. Review the selected property’s criteria before applying.

program_name: Transition Projects - SSVF (Supportive Services for Veteran Families)
notes: CARF accredited program.
description: Rapid rehousing and homelessness prevention for veterans and their families.
eligibility_summary: Served in U.S. Military; experiencing or at risk of homelessness; low-income.

notes: Complete the official shelter pre-screening form. Anyone unable to use the form may visit the Resource Center at 650 NW Irving Street. Shelter entry requires a reservation or referral; do not go directly to a shelter expecting a bed.
description: Access point for Transition Projects’ emergency and short-term shelters in Portland. Programs provide temporary shelter, meals, showers, laundry, case management, wellness support, and help moving toward permanent housing. Shelters are not available for drop-in entry; a reservation or referral is required.
eligibility_summary: Adults experiencing homelessness, including individuals and couples. Placement depends on bed availability and each shelter’s requirements. Some programs have specific eligibility based on household type, medical vulnerability, housing status, or sobriety expectations.

program_name: Urban League of Portland - Housing Department
notes: Call 503-280-2600 to ask which housing programs are accepting participants. The public page does not promise immediate rent assistance or a housing placement.
description: Culturally specific housing assistance that connects Black community members and others to stable housing resources and solutions.
eligibility_summary: People seeking housing stability support, with a focus on Black communities. Current program eligibility and openings are not listed on the public page; call the Urban League for screening information.

program_name: VA Portland Health Care - Homeless Veteran Care
notes: The National Call Center for Homeless Veterans is available 24/7 at 877-424-3838. Eligibility and enrollment vary by VA program.
description: Housing, health, benefits, and referral support for veterans who are homeless or at risk, including connection to the Portland Community Resource and Referral Center and HUD-VASH when eligible.
eligibility_summary: Veterans who are homeless or at risk of homelessness. Veterans, family members, friends, and supporters may call the national line for help connecting to services.

notes: Dial 211 or 866-698-6155 for help. As of January 1, 2026, 211info serves Oregon; Southwest Washington calls are handled by Washington 211.
description: A free, confidential statewide helpline and resource directory that connects people in all 36 Oregon counties with housing, shelter, food, utilities, health care, child care, transportation, and other services.
eligibility_summary: Anyone in Oregon seeking community-resource information or referrals.

program_name: Community Alliance of Tenants – Renters’ Rights Hotline
notes: CAT provides peer tenant education, not legal advice or rental-assistance funds. Hotline hours are limited and can change, so check the official hotline page before calling.
description: A tenant-education hotline that gives Oregon renters information about their rights and practical suggestions for protecting those rights.
eligibility_summary: Renters anywhere in Oregon. Callbacks outside funded counties may require CAT membership; check the official hotline page for current rules.

program_name: Just in Case Oregon - Free Mailed Naloxone
notes: Request supplies in advance; mailed orders are not an emergency response service. For an emergency, call 911. Contact info@justincaseoregon.org for order questions. Follow the instructions supplied with the medicine.
description: Request free nasal naloxone, a medicine that can reverse an opioid overdose, to be mailed in plain packaging. Use the program's online request form; instructions are included with the order.
eligibility_summary: People in Oregon with access to a mailing address that can receive the order. No prescription, ID check, or insurance is required. Agencies, organizations, and schools should use the separate bulk-ordering program linked on the provider's website.

notes: Complete the official online form or call the Eviction Defense line. Free language interpretation is available. Contact the program as soon as possible if court papers have been received.
description: Free legal help for Washington renters with low incomes who are facing eviction, including an online screening form and an eviction-defense phone line.
eligibility_summary: Renters with low income facing eviction anywhere in Washington. People with an eviction case in court may have a right to a free lawyer; screening determines available help.

notes: Complete the online form or call immediately. Have the eviction court case number and hearing date ready. Applicants must contact the project before their first appearance date.
description: Provides free legal assistance to low-income Oregon renters facing an eviction court case. The program may offer legal information, advice, or court representation after reviewing the case. Renters should contact the program immediately and before their first court appearance. This program does not provide rent assistance.
eligibility_summary: Low-income renters anywhere in Oregon with an active eviction court case. Multnomah County renters may also request help after receiving a landlord termination notice, even before a court case is filed. Services are available regardless of immigration status.

cost_details: Up to $3,200 over a 90-day assistance period, based on eligibility and needs. Payments go to approved providers or landlords, not unrestricted cash.
program_name: Oregon ODHS - Domestic Violence Relocation Assistance (TA-DVS)
notes: Contact a local ODHS office by phone or in person to apply. This is a specialized safety program, not general moving assistance for every low-income household. Approval and payment timing must be confirmed with ODHS.
description: Safety-related financial help for eligible domestic violence survivors. Assistance can cover housing or utility deposits, a moving truck, storage and essential replacement belongings.
eligibility_summary: Oregon residents who are pregnant, or are a parent or relative caring for a minor child, and face domestic violence now or a risk of it in the future. Household income must meet the program's limits; ODHS determines eligibility.

notes: Register through the current class calendar. Separate one-to-one coaching and on-demand courses may have fees; this listing is for the free live classes. Online classes provide access beyond the provider's Vancouver office.
description: Free classes on budgeting, saving, credit, banking, and managing debt. Online sessions and some in-person classes are available; visit the provider's calendar to choose a class and register.
eligibility_summary: Community members interested in financial education. The provider lists its live classes as free and open to the community; check each class for its format and registration instructions.

notes: One hotspot per household. The free data allowance is 200GB per year, not per month; optional extra data costs money. Availability is limited and mobile coverage varies. The program serves eligible households beyond Oregon and Washington as well.
description: A free mobile hotspot and 200GB of internet data per year for five years for eligible K-12 student households. A parent or guardian can apply directly through T-Mobile; this is not unlimited home internet.
eligibility_summary: Households with an eligible K-12 student. A parent or guardian must provide proof of eligibility through a qualifying program such as the National School Lunch Program, SNAP, Medicaid, Community Eligibility Provision, or Food Distribution Program on Indian Reservations. Check T-Mobile's current documentation and coverage requirements.

program_name: Tenants Union of Washington State – Tenants Rights Hotline
notes: The hotline offers free education and counseling from trained non-attorney counselors; it does not provide legal representation. Current hotline hours are Monday 10 AM–1 PM and Spanish Friday 9 AM–noon. Interpretation is available in most languages.
description: Free telephone counseling for Washington renters with eviction notices, landlord disputes, or other rental housing problems. Trained non-attorney counselors explain tenant rights, discuss steps that may help prevent housing loss, and provide referrals to community resources and legal assistance. The hotline does not provide legal advice or court representation.
eligibility_summary: Renters anywhere in Washington State who need information about eviction, landlord-tenant laws, notices, repairs, deposits, or other tenancy problems. No income requirement is stated.

cost_details: Up to $2,000 during one 30-day period, no more than once every 12 months. A prorated amount must be repaid if the family starts TANF within the following 12 months.
notes: Apply through Washington Connection, a local DSHS office, or by phone. This is not a guaranteed moving-company benefit; discuss the specific expense with DSHS before making arrangements.
description: Short-term financial assistance for eligible families who need help with housing, transportation or other essential expenses and do not need ongoing monthly TANF assistance.
eligibility_summary: Washington families who meet TANF or State Family Assistance eligibility but are not currently receiving either benefit, and expect to meet ongoing needs without monthly cash assistance. DSHS determines eligibility.

notes: Call Access Pierce or 211 for live support. Housing referrals are based on eligibility, vulnerability, and availability and are not guaranteed.
description: The first step for connecting with housing resources in Pierce County. Navigators discuss the household's situation, explore diversion options, and may place eligible households in the Priority Pool for matching with housing programs.
eligibility_summary: People in Pierce County who are experiencing homelessness or housing instability and need help identifying housing solutions. Eligibility and requirements vary by the program to which a household may be referred.

notes: Call the VOA Connect line to complete an eligibility assessment. If eligible, the household is referred to an appropriate navigation site; housing assistance is not guaranteed.
description: Connects Snohomish County households with homelessness prevention, housing navigation, program matching, and other services through a standardized screening and assessment process.
eligibility_summary: Individuals and families in Snohomish County who are experiencing homelessness, living in shelter or a place not meant for habitation, fleeing domestic violence, or at imminent risk of homelessness.

notes: Register for one or more classes using the provider's current schedule. For questions or help registering, call 971-226-9066 or email IDA@caowash.org. This is financial education, not a cash-assistance program.
description: Free online classes on budgeting, saving, banking, credit, and retirement. Choose a session on the provider's website and register to receive the class link by email.
eligibility_summary: Residents of Washington County, Oregon. Classes are held online, and Spanish interpreters are available in every class.

notes: Call Community Connect to discuss your situation. Eligible households may be assessed and connected to available services; an opening is not guaranteed.
description: Washington County's coordinated entry program for people who need housing or shelter support. Staff screen the household's situation, assess eligibility, and connect eligible callers with available housing, shelter, and support services.
eligibility_summary: People in Washington County who are experiencing homelessness or are at risk of becoming homeless. An assessment determines eligibility for particular programs, and housing or shelter is not guaranteed.
